subject: An empty `{}` as a list-operator argument parses as an empty ARRAY, not a hashref
description:
Found by an s374 probe while working #236 (the explain() renderer).

  perl: explain {}      -> {}          (hashref)
  PCL : explain {}      -> []          (empty array)

  perl: explain {a=>1}  -> { 'a' => 1 }   PCL: same          — already right
  perl: ref({})         -> HASH          PCL: HASH           — already right
  perl: sub f {ref $_[0]} f({})  -> HASH  PCL: HASH          — already right

So this is ONLY the empty-brace disambiguation after a list operator with no
parens: with content, the braces are read as a hash constructor; empty, they
are read as a block/empty list.  Perl's own heuristic reads an empty `{}` in
term position as an anonymous HASH.

Not a regression (pre-dates s374) and orthogonal to #236 — the renderer prints
`{}` correctly for every hashref that reaches it (probed with a variable, with
\%h, and with a non-empty literal).

Raised as ask 5.2 in docs/opus5-review-requests-s374.md.
